Adds no value over existing pages: The writing is clean, concrete and chronological. There are no hype words or em dashes. It opens with the Oneida reform-school story rather than a dictionary line, and it uses primary sources (NVIDIA's board bio, the CHM Fellow citation). But it does not answer the first target query, 'jensen huang idade': the metaTitle advertises age, yet neither the body nor the FAQ says he is 63 (born 17/02/1963, as of 26/10/2026). The style guide requires answering the search question on the first screen. Beyond that, the content matches the standard Wikipedia/Britannica timeline almost point for point. claims.claim: Born Jen-Hsun Huang on 17 February 1963 in Tainan, Taiwan (body, FAQ, person_json birthDate)
claims.note: Britannica gives the alias Jen-Hsun Huang and 'born February 17, 1963, Tainan, Taiwan'. Note: the Britannica page was served from a cache dated 2025-09-21 and still shows 'age 61'.

claims.claim: person_json birthPlace: Tainan, Taiwan
claims.note: Both sources give this. CHM: 'Born in 1963, in Tainan, Taiwan'.

claims.claim: The family moved to Thailand when he was five
claims.note: Britannica supports this ('When he was five, the family moved to Thailand'), but the sentence has no citation tag of its own. Add [s:britannica].

claims.claim: At about nine, he and his brother were sent to an uncle in Tacoma, Washington, who enrolled them at Oneida Baptist Institute in Kentucky
claims.note: Britannica confirms the age (nine), the uncle in Tacoma and Oneida Baptist Institute in Oneida, Kentucky.

claims.claim: Oneida Baptist Institute was a religious boarding school in Kentucky for boys considered 'problemáticos'
claims.note: Britannica calls it 'all-boys' and 'a religious reform school for "difficult" children'. 'Problemáticos' is a fair translation.

claims.claim: He arrived in the US from Thailand at nine, with his brother (lead, FAQ)
claims.note: Confirmed by Britannica. CHM also says he immigrated to the US at nine.

claims.claim: About two years later the parents arrived, took the boys out of the school and the family settled near Portland, Oregon
claims.note: Britannica: 'About two years later... settled in the suburbs of Portland, Oregon'.

claims.claim: Finished high school in Aloha in 1981
claims.note: Britannica says he attended Aloha High School and graduated in 1981.

claims.claim: Studied electrical engineering at Oregon State University and graduated in 1984
claims.note: Britannica confirms the bachelor's in EE from OSU in 1984. The NVIDIA bio also gives the BSEE from Oregon State.

claims.claim: Met Lori Mills at OSU and married her
claims.note: Britannica: 'At OSU, Huang met Lori Mills, a fellow engineering student, and the pair later married.' Reliable on-record source, and relevant because of the foundation.

claims.claim: Worked about a year at AMD, then at LSI Logic from 1985 to 1993, where he became director of a division
claims.note: NVIDIA bio: AMD 1984–1985, LSI Logic 1985–1993. Britannica: 'eventually become director of a company division'.

claims.claim: During that period (while working) he did a master's in electrical engineering at Stanford
claims.note: The NVIDIA bio confirms only the MSEE from Stanford, not when he did it. The timing 'nesse período' comes from Britannica ('While working, he returned to school...'). Add or swap the citation to [s:britannica].

claims.claim: In April 1993 he founded NVIDIA with engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem and was chosen to lead it
claims.note: Britannica: 'In April 1993... cofounded NVIDIA with fellow microchip designers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, who selected Huang to serve as CEO'. CHM confirms 1993 and the cofounders.

claims.claim: The trio started with $40,000; venture capital funds then put in $20 million
claims.note: Britannica: began with $40,000 and soon got $20 million from venture capital firms.

claims.claim: Since day one he has been president, CEO and a board member
claims.note: NVIDIA bio says he has served since inception as president, CEO and board member. A web search (GTC Berlin 2026 coverage, FY2026 filings) shows he is still CEO as of October 2026.

claims.claim: NVIDIA went public in 1999
claims.note: Britannica: 'The company went public in 1999.'

claims.claim: In 1999 NVIDIA launched the GeForce 256, billed as 'the world's first GPU', combining transform, lighting and rendering
claims.note: CHM: GeForce 256 in 1999, 'the world's first graphics processing unit', which 'combined transform, lighting, and rendering functions'.

claims.claim: CUDA was introduced in 2006, enabling general-purpose computing on NVIDIA GPUs
claims.note: Confirmed by CHM.

claims.claim: In 2012 AlexNet was trained on NVIDIA GPUs and the company pivoted to accelerated computing for AI
claims.note: CHM: GPUs 'used in 2012 to power the breakthrough AlexNet', after which the company pivoted to AI with accelerated computing. 'Treinada' is a reasonable reading.

claims.claim: In 2018 Huang said GPU performance was growing faster than Moore's law predicts, and the press called it 'Huang's law'
claims.note: Britannica: remark made at GTC 2018 (GPUs 25 times faster than five years earlier), which the press dubbed 'Huang's law'.

claims.claim: Fortune named him Businessperson of the Year in 2017
claims.note: NVIDIA bio: 'In 2017, he was named Fortune's Businessperson of the Year.'

claims.claim: Harvard Business Review ranked him the world's best-performing CEO in 2019
claims.note: NVIDIA bio: HBR ranked him No. 1 on its 2019 list of the 100 best-performing CEOs.

claims.claim: Time included him among the 100 most influential people in 2021
claims.note: Confirmed by Britannica. The claim is still true, but the section is incomplete: a web search shows he was on the Time 100 again in 2024, was among Time's 2025 Person of the Year ('Architects of AI') and was the FT's Person of the Year 2025. Not a factual error. Adding these with primary citations is up to the editor.

claims.claim: Named a Computer History Museum Fellow in 2024
claims.note: CHM profile: '2024 Fellow', for visionary leadership in graphics, accelerated computing and AI.

claims.claim: With his wife he created the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation in 2007
claims.note: Britannica: 'In 2007 Huang and his wife founded the philanthropic Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation'.

claims.claim: Summary/knownFor: Taiwan-born engineer, cofounder of NVIDIA in 1993, its president and CEO ever since; GeForce 256 in 1999 presented as the first GPU; AI focus from 2012
claims.note: Front matter has no citations, but each element repeats a cited, verified body claim (nvidia-bio, chm, britannica).

claims.claim: FAQ: Huang, Malachowsky and Priem founded NVIDIA in April 1993; Huang was CEO from the start
claims.note: Supported by Britannica and the NVIDIA bio, as cited in the body.

claims.claim: FAQ: EE degree from Oregon State in 1984 and master's in EE from Stanford
claims.note: Supported by Britannica, the NVIDIA bio and CHM.
